newsitem.title: PERU: Peru bolsa seen healthy despite problems.
newsitem.headline: Peru bolsa seen healthy despite problems.

text.p: Peru's encouraging economic prospects will offset the negative influence of climatic and political problems to give the Lima Stock Exchange moderate growth in July, brokers said.

"The economic factor weighs more on investors," said Julio Alcalde, analyst for MGS and Associates brokerages. "However, we must follow closely some factors that could stunt (the market's) growth, like the climatic phenomenon El Nino and the political problems confronting the government."

The government's tumbling popularity for its perceived authoritarianism, and the anticipated damage to agriculture, fishing and infrastructure from the emerging El Nino weather pattern, began to concern investors in June.

But the government insists the economy is still on track for at least five percent growth this year, up from 2.8 percent in 1996. And analysts say El Nino is unlikely to have a major impact on gross domestic product this year.
"A five percent growth at the year's end is the worst-case scenario and that is not bad for investors," said a broker at Lima-based T&J. "They know ... in what sectors to invest."

Manuel Torres, from Finvest, said drinks and ice-cream companies would benefit in July from the unusually high temperatures. "Also, polymetallic mining companies should see benefits because of the strength of zinc," he added.
Investors will also be interested in the construction sector, because of possible high demand for materials to repair damages from floods caused by El Nino, Torres said.
Brokers predicted the most attractive individual stocks in July will be Cementos Norte Pacasmayo, Cementos Lima, zinc producer Perubar and mining company Atacocha.
Also popular will be the shares of food company Alicorp, brewery Cerveceria Backus y Johnston and ice-cream producer D'Onofrio, as well as miner Estano Minsur, they added.
Other factors in play during July will be half-year corporate results, second half macroeconomic forecasts, and President Alberto Fujimori's mid-year policy message.
The bolsa's general index rose 1.25 percent in June while the blue-chip index lost 0.06 percent. Both gained 50.80 percent and 53.96 percent respectively in the first half.

Despite the low gains in June, the high profits of the previous months, especially in the polymetallic sector, ensured good trading volume. Analysts said this was another sign of investor confidence in the economy.

According to latest bolsa figures, the highest growth sector between January and June was mining labor shares with a 178.56 percent gain. Common mining stock rose 87.40 percent overall, common industrial 44.03 percent and brewers 43.03 percent. Among other sectors, bank shares rose 36.89 percent, industrial labor stocks 33.48 percent and public services 25.86 percent.

"In July investors will closely follow the evolution of companies for the second half. I believe it will be a month of slow growth, since the companies' balance accounts will start appearing around mid-month," said Eder Egusquiza, from the stock house Finanval.
